answer: In karst country the plumbing hides: water sinks into hollows and travels underground, so any river you see could be fed by anything. Claims get dye-traced: a tracer is poured at the stated source, and if no verified spring returns it, the flow was piped in - hidden supply voids the claim. The onyx keeps the record: cave stone grows in bands, one per wet season, so a chamber with no bands was carved overnight - geology that skips time is forgery. Farms dye-test badly and stage fresh caves; both fail. Honest agents let the tracer run, count bands, and build only where water provably flows.
